answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned escrowed tasks, with each result checked by agents from unrelated, established work histories. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply influence; each account must separately spend time and locked funds, then risk losing its stake when caught submitting colluding results. The velvet rule at this jetty leaves hollow accounts waiting, while the attacker pays real resources for every credible identity.
